NJD.body: New Jersey has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Canadiens can make it interesting if they get good looks.

story.head: Bratt’s favorite opponent
paras: The Devils have won two in a row, while the Canadiens (12-5-4) lost 3-1 to the Rangers on Monday. Going in, the Habs are third in the Atlantic (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Devils second in the Metropolitan (tied for fourth).
The Canadiens’ record (.667) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.547), largely because they’re 7-5 in one-goal games. The Devils’ record (.714) is about what their chances are worth.

The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but take more penalties than they draw (30th). The Devils, by contrast, keep things calm after the whistle (3rd lowest). They also rarely throw hits (2nd lowest) and draw more penalties than they take (3rd). Something has to give when the Canadiens’ shooting runs into the Devils’ defense, and the Devils’ power play (7th) could do real damage against the Canadiens’ penalty kill (23rd).

Cole Caufield (12 G / 7 A / 19 P in 21 GP) is tied for the Canadiens’ scoring lead. Lane Hutson (3 G / 16 A / 19 P in 21 GP) shares it. For the Devils, Jack Hughes (10 G / 17 A / 27 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in six straight games against Montréal. Jesper Bratt (4 G / 17 A / 21 P in 21 GP) is next in line.

Jacob Fowler (9-2-2 / .923 SV% in 13 GS) has been a rock in net for Montréal and is expected to start. Connor Hellebuyck (7-0-0 / .916 SV% in 7 GS) has been a rock in net for New Jersey and is expected to start.

items.text: Connor Hellebuyck has won all seven of his starts this season, already the longest winning run to open a season by any goalie in franchise history.
The Canadiens are newly without Chris Kreider and Josh Anderson, and have been without Ivan Demidov and Samuel Montembeault for several games. Jacob Fowler is expected to start.
The Devils have been without Anthony Mantha since Nov 7.
Brett Pesce has missed the Devils’ last two games.
